whyChose.heading: Why we chose this boat.
whyChose.body: We spent nearly a year looking at catamarans before we found Tropicalia. She's sleeker and has a longer waterline than most of the newer production cats we considered. She has less windage, a better motion through waves, and good bridgedeck clearance. The cockpit feels enclosed and safe with kids aboard. The galley is a real kitchen, not an afterthought. And the bulkheads and furniture are fiberglassed into the hull—not just glued—so nothing creaks or shifts. The [Voyage Yachts factory](https://www.voyageyachts.com/) in South Africa custom built her for private owners in 2010, and she is the youngest 500 model in the fleet.

alternatingSections.heading: A 50-foot bluewater owner's version catamaran.
alternatingSections.body: Tropicalia is a three-cabin owner's version with the range and capacity to cruise anywhere. Fifty feet gives her real storage—water, food, fuel, tools, spares, dive equipment, and all the rest of your gear. Under sail she has a long waterline and a full-batten main on a Harken Battcar system. At anchor, 800W of solar, a 4kW Onan sound-insulated generator, Mabru air conditioning, a washing machine, and Starlink keep daily life easy.

alternatingSections.heading: Room to live your best cruising life.
alternatingSections.body: At 27 feet of beam, the main salon feels big, open, and airy. The salon and galley flow into the cockpit via sliding glass doors so meals, movie nights, and long evenings at anchor all happen in the same open space. The galley is a full kitchen with a proper gas cooktop and oven, and there is a 4-seat bar for casual meals and entertaining. The entire starboard hull is the owner's suite—king berth, private head with a large stall shower, office area, a walk-in closet, and real storage everywhere. The port hull features two queen cabins with private heads and a laundry area. Underway, the long waterline gives her an easy, level motion that lets everyone keep functioning in bigger seas. On deck, she carries a 12.5-foot Zodiac with a 25hp outboard, so shore runs and snorkel trips are quick and dry.

alternatingSections.heading: Tropicalia is a well-equipped cruising machine.
alternatingSections.body: Tropicalia was custom built by [Voyage Yachts in South Africa](https://www.voyageyachts.com/) with bulkheads and furniture fiberglassed into the hull—one solid structure that doesn't creak or shift underway. She is energy- and water-independent, with 800 watts of solar panels, new 1,280ah lithium batteries, a 4kW Onan generator, a reliable new watermaker, and ample tankage. She has lots of cruising comforts, like a dedicated laundry room, an office, a giant two-door chest freezer, a separate refrigerator, and dual-zone Mabru air conditioning, including a 12V unit that can be run on the batteries, and all-electric winches. Dual 110v and 220v Victron chargers/inverters and dual shore power inlets mean she can cruise anywhere in the world. She carries a new 6-person offshore life raft, a new EPIRB, AIS man-overboard beacons on every life jacket, and a full Raymarine radar, Axiom chartplotter (2025), and autopilot suite (2025), for offshore navigation.

features.title: Electronics & Navigation
features.description: New Raymarine Axiom 12" chartplotter with full Caribbean and North America cartography, plus an Orca navigation display that's removable from the nav station and can move to the helm. Forward-looking and side-scan sonar. Predict Wind Hub for position tracking via Starlink.
features.body:
Everything you need to navigate is new, and everything is integrated. The core is a Raymarine Axiom+ 12" chartplotter with a complete Navionics cartography package — the US east coast, the Caribbean, and down into South America. We also added an Orca Display 2 nav display mounted in a self-charging cradle at the nav station but detachable, so you can carry it out to the helm when you want instruments in your hands. It's interfaced with the NMEA2000-connected Orca Core 2 system to tie it into the boat's other electronics and works as either a chartplotter or an instrument display.

We also installed a [Predict Wind Data Hub](https://www.predictwind.com/datahub), which uploads our position via Starlink in real time — friends and family can [follow our boat on our blog](https://sailingtropicalia.com/location/) without us having to manually update our position.

**New electronics (installed by** [**the Boat Doctor**](https://boatdrusa.com/) **in St. Augustine):**

- Raymarine Axiom+ 12" MFD chartplotter — with North America + Caribbean + South America cartography
- Orca Display 2 and Orca Core 2 — Display is removable from the nav station, can move to the helm; interfaced with Raymarine; also shows AIS enriched AIS targets via Starlink (a great safety feature)
- New control pad and computer for the autopilot
- Predict Wind Hub — position tracking via Starlink

**Existing Raymarine integrated system:**

- Raymarine RD418HD Radome (Fall 2023)
- Raymarine ST60 Tridata and Wind Indicator
- Raymarine ST7002 Autopilot with LewMar Rotary Drive
- Raymarine RAY55E VHF Radio with remote speaker in salon
- Raymarine AIS650 Class B Transponder with dedicated antenna
- 2× Raymarine GPS with external antennas
- Handheld Raymarine and Icom VHF radios

**Sonar & other:**

- Windlass remote and chain counter at the helm

The boat is wired for both 110V and 220V and has two shore power inlets, so wherever you tie up — US, Caribbean, Europe — you can plug in. On top of that, there are separate Victron inverter/chargers for each voltage: a 3000W 230V unit and a Multiplus 12/3000 120/50. That means any appliance you bring aboard from any region just works, and the charger side keeps the lithium bank topped up from shore or generator.

- Onan 4kW genset — fully gone over, new hoses and parts

features.title: DC Electrical & Lithium Battery Bank
features.description: Four LiTime 12V 320Ah Mini Bluetooth LiFePO4 batteries (1,280Ah / ~16.4 kWh) — professionally installed by marine electricians in St. Augustine with extra safety cutoffs. 200A BMS per battery with Bluetooth monitoring. 800W of well-positioned solar, secondary high-output alternators, and days of capacity under normal loads.
features.body:
The new 1,280Ah lithium house bank is four LiTime 12V 320Ah Mini Bluetooth LiFePO4 batteries wired in parallel — about 16.4 kWh of usable capacity. Each battery has its own 200A BMS, IP65-rated enclosure, and a Bluetooth 5.0 app that shows state-of-charge, cell voltages, and temperature in real time. They were professionally installed by marine electricians in St. Augustine, with additional safety cutoffs and kill switches added on top of the factory BMS — a belt-and-suspenders setup. Fully charged, the bank holds for days under normal cruising loads.

The solar panels are positioned well — on the coach roof and bimini — so they avoid most of the usual shading issues and routinely put out close to their rated output. The engines also carry secondary high-output alternators, so any time you're motoring you're charging the bank hard. Between solar, alternators, and a short generator run every few days to make water, we rarely think about power.

- 4× LiTime 12V 320Ah Mini Bluetooth LiFePO4 batteries (1,280Ah / ~16.4 kWh total, upgraded from 1,100Ah at purchase)
- 200A BMS per battery (2,560W continuous per battery; 1,000A peak for 1 second)
- Bluetooth 5.0 monitoring via LiTime app — real-time SOC, cell voltages, temperature
- IP65 enclosure, 4,000+ cycles at 100% DOD (15,000+ at 60% DOD), 5-year warranty
- Professionally installed by marine electricians in St. Augustine — extra safety cutoffs and kill switches beyond factory BMS

features.title: Rainman Modular AC-140 Watermaker
features.description: Rainman Modular AC-140 HighOutput — up to 37 GPH (26–37 depending on water temp) from two 40" Dow Filmtec RO membranes. Properly plumbed into the boat so you can fill each tank individually and pickle in place without buckets or hose gymnastics.
features.body:
Installed new by us. The Rainman Modular AC-140 HighOutput is the top unit in their AC line — two 40″ Dow Filmtec RO membranes, a 316 stainless steel General Pump high-pressure pump, and a Jabsco lift pump. Production runs 26–37 gallons per hour depending on water temperature, and the whole system draws about 1,300 watts in steady state — easy work for the generator or the 3kW Victron inverter.

A lot of Rainman installs are bucket-and-hose setups — great when you buy the unit, less great five years in when you're pickling it on deck in a crosswind. We plumbed ours properly into the boat from day one. You can fill either water tank individually with production water, and when the boat sits for a while you pickle the system by adding chemical to its own reservoir — no buckets, no disassembly.

- Rainman Modular AC-140 HighOutput — installed new in December of 2025
- Up to 37 GPH (26–37 depending on water temperature)
- Two 40" Dow Filmtec RO membranes
- 316 stainless steel General Pump WMR high-pressure pump
- Jabsco impeller lift pump with TEFC induction motor
- 230V
- \~1,300W steady-state draw — runs comfortably off the generator or the 3kW Victron
- Plumbed directly into the boat's freshwater system
- Fill either tank individually with fresh production water
- Pickle-in-place via the unit's own reservoir — add chemical, run, done
- Five 5-micron pleated paper pre-filter cartridges included; non-proprietary consumables
- Supplements 211 gallons of tank capacity

features.title: Extended Rear Deck, Sugar Scoops & Exterior
features.description: Original owners nearly doubled the standard rear deck — you can walk all the way around when the dinghy is in its chocks. Hot and cold showers in both sugar scoops, deep lockers sized for dive tanks, and a sleek, low-windage profile.
features.body:
The original owners were aerospace-engineer types who specified this boat to a higher standard than the production spec sheet. The rear deck was extended nearly double — meaning you can still walk from one sugar scoop to the other even with the dinghy in its chocks. It becomes its own back porch: a place to sit, dry gear, and relax without ever having to move the tender.

Each sugar scoop has hot-and-cold freshwater showers right where you come back aboard from the beach, and the stern lockers are deep enough to double as dive-tank storage.

- Rear deck extended by nearly 2× standard — walk-around access with dinghy in chocks
- Hot and cold freshwater showers in both sugar scoops
- Deep stern storage lockers — rated for dive tanks
- All new graphics on both bows
- Carbon fiber vinyl wrap around front windows

features.title: Five Remote-Work Spaces
features.description: Private office in the owner's cabin, a proper nav station, a full salon dinette, a 4-seat bar with stools, and an outdoor cockpit table. Real workspaces — built for a family that homeschooled and worked from the water.
features.body:
Designed for a family that works from the water. We ran a business, homeschooled two kids, and held team meetings from this boat across a full Caribbean cruising season. Five distinct workspaces mean multiple people can take calls, focus, or just hang out at the same time without treading on each other — and each spot has power, Wi-Fi, and airflow.

- Private desk in the starboard owner's cabin — a real one, not a laptop corner. Power and ventilation at the seat.
- Nav / chart station in the salon with full storage underneath — wired for 12V, 115V, and USB. We used this for homeschooling every day.
- Main salon U-shaped settee with pedestal table — seats six
- Bar top with Corian work surface and four stools — a natural laptop zone with the galley right behind you
- Outdoor cockpit table with cushioned seating under the bimini
- 12V and USB outlets at every station — office, nav area, cockpit, windlass locker
- Thermostat-controlled 12V cooling and ventilation fans throughout

features.description: New Fire TV in the salon connected to Starlink, a second TV in the owner's cabin, and speakers wired literally everywhere — indoors, cockpit, stern, and up the mast — driven by a salon amplifier.
features.body:
The whole boat is wired for sound — speakers in the salon, cockpit, stern, and wake-tower speakers on the mast spreader — all driven by a proper amplifier. Family movie nights happen in the salon on a new flat-screen Fire TV that's connected to Starlink, so you can stream whatever you would at home. There's also a TV in the owner's cabin on the same Wi-Fi, and a local antenna for broadcast if you'd rather.

- New Fire TV in the salon — connected to Starlink, streams whatever you want
- Second flat-screen TV in the owner's cabin — also on Wi-Fi

quote.text: Pull the dinghy right up to the back of the cat, connect the hose, and refill from a big aluminum tank onboard. Fill it once at the beginning of the season and you're set.

features.description: Zodiac 12.5' YL380DL center console with new Hypalon tubes, Suzuki 25hp 4-stroke (<100 hours), and a built-in dinghy refill system — an onboard aluminum gas tank in the starboard sugar scoop with a hose to fill the dinghy without ever going ashore.
features.body:
The dinghy gets used hard on a cruising boat, and this one is set up accordingly. A full-size Zodiac 12.5' with center console and wheel, electric start, electric trim, and a 25hp 4-stroke with fewer than 100 hours on it — gets on plane, hauls four adults, and covers real distance.

The hidden gem: the original owners specified an auxiliary aluminum gasoline tank built into the starboard sugar scoop with a filler hose. You pull the dinghy up to the stern, connect the hose, and refill from the boat. Top off the main tank once a season and you never think about dinghy gas again.

- Zodiac 12.5' YL380DL center console dinghy with new Hypalon tubes
- Suzuki 25hp 4-stroke outboard — electric start, electric trim, under 100 hours
- Onboard aluminum auxiliary gas tank in the starboard sugar scoop — with refill hose for the dinghy
- Tachometer / speedometer, running lights, bilge pump
- Teak aft platform with integral dinghy chocks
- Boom extension for dinghy lift halyard (acts as secondary main halyard)

quote.speaker: alex
quote.text: This is our second Caribbean cruise. The first was without a washing machine. The second has been with one. It just makes everything easier.

features.title: Laundry Aboard — With Sheltered Drying Lines
features.description: Samsung automatic washing machine plumbed in, plus drying lines mounted under the cockpit roof so your clothes stay dry through a squall. This is the upgrade that changes how long a family can stay out.
features.body:
This is our second long Caribbean cruise. Our first one was without a washing machine. Our second is with one. The difference is enormous — laundromat runs used to eat a whole day every week and forced us into marinas or towns we didn't want to be in. Now we anchor wherever we want, for as long as we want.

And we rigged permanent drying lines under the cockpit roof — clothes stay out of the rain, so a passing squall doesn't restart your laundry day.

- Samsung automatic washing machine — full cycle, plumbed in
- Located in the port-hull corridor so it doesn't dominate a cabin
- Runs on 120V shore or inverter power from the 1,280Ah lithium house bank
- Dedicated drying lines mounted under the cockpit roof — dry in any weather

features.title: Master Head & Shower
features.description: Large head in the owner's cabin with a separate spacious shower stall and a new electric toilet with freshwater flush.
features.body:
The previous owners converted the owner's cabin head to a composting toilet, which means no blackwater tank on the starboard side, no joker valves, and no smells.

- Composting toilet — dry head, no blackwater plumbing
- Separate spacious walk-in shower stall with stainless grab rails
- Pressurized hot and cold fresh water
- Remote VHF command microphone / speaker
- Remote generator start / stop from the master
- Overhead opening hatch for ventilation

features.title: Guest Heads (×2)
features.description: Two ensuite guest heads in the port hull — each with electric flush toilets (one new), pressurized hot and cold water, and a new overboard discharge pump for the holding tank.
features.body:
Each port-side guest cabin has its own private ensuite head. The plumbing in the port hull has been fully overhauled — one of the electric flush toilets is brand new, and a new overboard discharge pump was installed on the holding tank.

- 2× electric flush toilets — one of them new
- New overboard discharge pump on the holding tank
- 2× pressurized hot and cold freshwater showers and sinks
- 2× integrated hand basins with extendable mixer
- 2× vanity cabinets with mirror and stainless towel rails
- 2× toiletries storage cupboards
- Red LED night lights in each head
- 2× IsoTemp water heaters (fully serviced 2023)
- Port hull blackwater keel tank

features.title: Ventilation & Hatches
features.description: Large overhead opening hatches throughout, Nicro solar-powered vent fans, 12V circulation fans in every cabin, and thermostat-controlled engine-room ventilation.
features.body:
Passive and active airflow was a priority in the build and subsequent upgrades. Every berth has a hatch above it; every cabin has a fan; every hull has keep-cool airflow even at anchor with no power.

- Large overhead opening hatches with Nicro solar ventilation fans
- 2× circulation fans in the master cabin
- 12V ventilation fans in both guest cabins
- Thermostat-controlled 12V cooling / ventilation fans in living spaces
- Thermostat-controlled engine-room ventilation fans in both hulls
- Overhead and bulkhead-mounted LED spot lights (white / red) for night ventilation without glare

features.title: Cabin & Mood Lighting
features.description: LED everything — multi-color selectable spreader lights, red/white spot lights in the salon, red night lights in the heads, new salon fixtures, and dimmable backlit name plates.
features.body:
- Overhead and bulkhead-mounted LED spot lights (white or red) in the salon
- New salon lighting and fixtures
- LED reading and overhead lights in the master cabin
- LED overhead + bulkhead reading lights in guest cabins
- Red LED night lights in the heads for low-impact eyes-adjusted use
- LED lighting in spreaders — multi-color selectable (blue & white)
- Courtesy lights in engine room, lazarette, hull steps (red), sugarscoop steps (blue)
- Custom LED-backlit vessel name plates on a dimmer
- Photocell auto anchor light (on/off control)

features.title: Refrigeration
features.description: Dual 12V Adler Barbour units — one dedicated air-cooled freezer and one digital-control refrigerator — plus a second cockpit fridge for drinks. Independent of shore power.
features.body:
- 12V Adler Barbour freezer — air-cooled, digital control
- 12V Adler Barbour refrigerator with digital controls
- Cockpit refrigerator — separate, for drinks and quick-access
- All refrigeration runs off 12V DC directly from the 1,280Ah lithium house bank

features.title: Life Raft — New
features.description: Brand-new 6-person Offshore Commander life raft (valise model) — replaced by current owners. Current certification.
features.body:
The life raft is one of the most important — and most commonly overlooked — pieces of safety gear on any offshore boat. Old rafts fail their inspections and get quietly shelved. This one was replaced new by the current owners, so the next owner is not starting behind the line.

- New 6-person Offshore Commander life raft — valise model (not cradle-mounted)
- Current certification
- Paired with a fully stocked ditch bag (see Emergency Beacons & Ditch Bag)

quote.speaker: eric
quote.text: If you have kids, this matters. The beacon auto-deploys when it hits the water — the child doesn't have to remember anything. It transmits their position back to the boat as an AIS target and you can go right to them.

features.title: Safety Gear — With AIS Man-Overboard Beacons
features.description: New life raft, new EPIRB, stocked ditch bag, in-date flares, and AIS man-overboard beacons on every life jacket. The beacons auto-deploy when they hit water — critical if your kid is the one in the drink.
features.body:
A brand-new life raft and EPIRB are the headline items, but the upgrade we care about most is a set of AIS-enabled man-overboard beacons built into each of our four life jackets.

Most offshore beacons require the wearer to activate them manually. These don't — the antenna deploys automatically the moment the jacket hits saltwater, and the beacon transmits the swimmer's position back to the boat as an AIS target on the chart plotter. If your kid goes over, they don't have to remember anything. You can steer straight to them.

- New life raft
- New EPIRB in the ditch bag
- AIS-enabled man-overboard beacons on all four life jackets — auto-deploy on water contact, transmit position to the boat as AIS targets
- Personal locator beacons (PLBs)
- New ditch bag stocked for offshore abandonment
- Current, in-date flare kit
- Handheld Raymarine and Icom VHFs in the ditch bag rotation
- Plenty of life jackets and secondary safety gear

features.title: Fire Suppression
features.description: Fireboy XINTEX automatic fire extinguisher in the engine rooms plus high water alarms and 12V bilge pumps throughout.
features.body:
- Fireboy XINTEX automatic fire extinguisher (heat-activated, engine rooms)
- Manual fire extinguishers throughout the boat
- 12V bilge pumps with high-water alarms
- Escape hatch in the main forward salon

features.title: Yanmar Diesels + 2025 Saildrives & Auto Props
features.description: Reliable Yanmars paired with brand-new SD60 saildrives (2025) and rebuilt Brunton Auto Props. Seven knots at 1,500 RPM in flat water. Can cross an ocean on one engine at a time.
features.body:
Most 15-year-old diesels hide deferred maintenance. These don't. The Yanmars were brought down to the frames: rebuilt alternators, every hose and belt replaced, new motor mounts, serviced heat exchangers, engine rooms repainted so any future drip is obvious at a glance. The saildrives are brand-new SD60 units installed in 2025, and the Brunton Auto Props were sent back to the factory rep for new bearings and service.

The combination is genuinely efficient. Seven knots of boat speed at 1,500 RPM in flat conditions — and because she's designed around a long 50' waterline, she runs very happily on one engine. On an ocean crossing you can alternate engines and still hold six knots cruising. Top speed under power is about nine knots.

When you turn the engines off, the Brunton props feather automatically — put them in gear, they lock, and you pick up roughly another knot of sailing speed compared to fixed props.

- 2× Yanmar 3JH5E 40hp diesels — brought down to the frames by current owners
- 2× brand-new SD60 saildrives (2025)
- 2× Brunton 460mm (18") self-pitching auto propellers — sent back to factory rep, new bearings, fully serviced (2025)
- Props feather automatically when engines are locked off — ~1 kt sailing speed vs fixed props
- 7 kts @ 1,500 RPM flat water, ~9 kts top
- Runs happily on one engine for ocean crossings — ~6 kts cruising
- All hoses and belts replaced
- Both alternators rebuilt (July 2023)
- Stainless steel motor mounts
- Heat exchangers serviced
- Engine rooms fully repainted — clean, inspection-ready
- 2× 80A Yanmar alternators + 2× 120A AMPLE high-output alternators feeding the house bank
- 2× WS500 external regulators (new Oct 2021)
- 3× Racor 500FG fuel filters
- Approx. 2,800 engine hours (hour meters are known to be inaccurate)
- Last oil change: April 2024
- New zincs at sale

features.title: New Saildrives & Rebuilt Props (2025)
features.description: Brand-new SD60 saildrives and fully rebuilt Bruton 18-inch self-pitching auto propellers — both installed in 2025. Zero deferred drivetrain maintenance.
features.body:
Saildrives and propellers are the two drivetrain items that quietly rack up five-figure bills at survey time. Both were done new in 2025 — before the boat ever went on the FSBO market.

- 2× new SD60 saildrives (2025)
- 2× Bruton 460mm (18") self-pitching auto propellers — fully rebuilt in 2025
- 3-blade bronze construction
- Self-pitching design adjusts automatically for motoring vs sailing
- New zincs at sale

features.title: Onan 4kW Genset — Gone-Over, Remote-Controlled
features.description: 4kW diesel generator, fully torn down and serviced with new hoses and parts. Directly powers the watermaker and washing machine. Start/stop in the owner's cabin plus a remote electronic panel at the nav station.
features.body:
The generator has been fully torn down and gone over — new hoses and a long list of new parts — and runs beautifully. With the lithium bank and 800W of solar doing most of the day-to-day work, we typically only fire the genset every few days to make water. When we do, it also powers the washing machine and keeps the bank topped up.

Start it from the owner's cabin or from the remote electronic panel at the nav station without ever leaving your seat.

- Onan 4kW diesel genset — fully torn down and serviced, new hoses and parts
- Approx. 4,615 hours
- Directly powers the Rainman watermaker and the washing machine
- Integrated into the Victron charging system
- Remote start/stop switch in the owner's cabin
- Remote electronic panel at the nav station

features.title: 800W Solar — Positioned to Actually Work
features.description: Two 400W panels mounted on the coach roof and bimini where they avoid most of the usual shading traps, so they routinely put out close to their rated output. Covers daily house loads at anchor.
features.body:
Solar is the difference between anchoring out for a weekend and anchoring out for a month. Where a lot of boats stick panels wherever they fit — and then watch the boom, the radar arch, or the mast throw shade across them half the day — these are positioned on the coach roof and bimini to stay in the sun. We routinely see close to rated output.

- 2× 400W solar panels (800W total) — coach roof and bimini mounted (2022)
- Positioned to minimize shading from the boom, mast, and arch
- EPEVER Tracer 4215BN 40A MPPT charge controller
- MT50 remote display
- Feeds the 1,280Ah LiFePO4 house bank directly

features.title: D400 Wind Generator
features.description: A D400 wind generator — widely regarded as the quietest cruising wind gen on the market — supplements solar when it's cloudy or after dark.
features.body:
Solar gives you a lot, but not at night and not in rain squalls. The D400 fills the gap. It's known for being one of the few wind generators you can actually sleep under.

- D400 wind generator — the quiet one
- Stop/run dump resistor (required with lithium banks)
- Charges the 1,100Ah LiFePO4 house bank
- Runs 24/7 — especially valuable in trade-wind anchorages

features.title: Mainsail
features.description: Full-batten mainsail with a large roach on a Harken Batt-Car track, a new stack pack from the Voyage factory, and full lazy-jack rigging.
features.body:
The main is fully battened with a large roach, riding on a Harken Batt-Car track for low-friction hoisting and dropping. Two reef points. A factory-new stack pack from Voyage and lazy jacks handle everything when you drop the sail — no scramble on deck.

- Full-batten mainsail with large roach
- Harken Batt-Car track system — low-friction hoist and drop
- New stack pack from the Voyage factory
- Full lazy-jack rigging
- Two reef points
- Double-purchase main halyard

features.title: Headsails: Genoa + Self-Tacking Jib
features.description: 130% furling genoa plus a small self-tacking furling jib for heavy wind or slowing things down at night. Both on Profurl furlers. Shorthanded-ready.
features.body:
A cruising catamaran really wants two headsails: a big reaching/downwind genoa for light air, and a small self-tacking jib for upwind work, heavy weather, or — practically speaking — when you want to slow the boat down at night and sleep better. Both are on furlers, so neither decision requires going forward on a pitching deck.

- 130% furling genoa with UV cover
- Small self-tacking furling jib (doubles as a storm jib) with UV cover
- Both on Profurl furlers
- Two reefing lines and luff pendants

features.title: Code Zero & Spinnaker Rigging
features.description: Dedicated halyards for a Code Zero/screecher and a symmetric spinnaker, plus a bow sprit attachment point. Off-wind gear ready to fly.
features.body:

- Dedicated spinnaker halyard
- Bow sprit attachment point

features.title: Mast & Standing Rigging
features.description: Anodized aluminum triple-spreader mast with full Harken hardware. Pulled and stored on the hard every hurricane season for inspection — rigger has replaced elements as needed over the boat's life.
features.body:
The mast has been pulled and stored on the hard every hurricane season for inspection. Any rigging components that needed replacement have been replaced as the rigger has called them out — so the standing rigging isn't all from one year, but nothing has been left in service longer than it should.

- Harken mast hardware throughout

- Intermediate + cap shrouds

- Harken 5:1 mainsheet on a full-width curved track
- Spinlock rope clutches
- Masthead Windex
- Mast pulled and stored on the hard each hurricane season for inspection and maintenance

features.body:

features.title: Redundant Autopilot
features.description: Two independent Raymarine ST7002 autopilot heads on two different drive systems — a WHITLOCK and a Lewmar rotary. Lose one, the other takes over.
features.body:
Autopilot failure is one of the most common offshore breakdowns. This boat has two complete systems wired in parallel. If the primary drive fails mid-passage, the backup is already there.

- 2× Raymarine ST7002 autopilot control heads
- WHITLOCK drive + Lewmar rotary drive — two independent actuators
- Raymarine X3 autopilot corepack
- Integrated with chartplotter, wind instruments, and AIS

features.title: Radar & AIS
features.description: Raymarine RD418HD digital radome (Fall 2023) plus AIS650 Class B transceiver with dedicated antenna. See and be seen, day or night, clear or fog.

- Raymarine C120W Multifunction Display

- Dedicated AIS antenna (separate from VHF)

features.title: Forward-Looking & Side Sonar
features.description: Pantopix forward-looking and side-scan sonar (installed Feb 2023) integrated with a Garmin chartplotter display. See reef heads and shallow spots before you find them the hard way.
features.body:
Traditional depth sounders only tell you what's directly under the hull — by the time a reef shows up, you've already hit it. Forward-looking sonar shows you what's ahead.

- Pantopix forward-looking sonar
- Side-scan sonar
- Installed February 2023
- Integrated with Garmin chartplotter display

features.title: Starlink Maritime + Backup Starlink Mini
features.description: Motorized Starlink dish (tilts and rotates for best signal) mounted on the bimini, plus an unopened Starlink Mini in the box as a backup unit. Full broadband at anchor, underway, and offshore.
features.body:
Starlink changed cruising. Passages that used to be weather-report-and-hope are now live-radar-and-GRIB. Anchorages that used to be sat-phone-only are now video-call-with-grandma. And for anyone with remote work, this one piece of equipment is the difference between a sabbatical and a lifestyle.

The boat has the motorized Starlink dish — the one with built-in actuators that tilt and rotate the antenna to keep a lock on the constellation regardless of how the boat's heading. It's mounted on the bimini and runs on 12V directly from the house bank, so it stays online without starting the generator. A brand-new Starlink Mini comes with the boat — still sealed in the box — as a backup or secondary unit.

- Motorized Starlink dish (automatic tilt/rotate actuators) mounted on the bimini
- Runs on 12V from the house bank — no generator needed
- Full broadband at anchor, underway, or offshore
- Brand-new Starlink Mini included — unopened, still sealed — as a backup unit
- Installed by current owners (post-purchase upgrade — not in the original broker listing)

quote.speaker: eric
quote.text: The helm is in the cockpit, slightly elevated — not up out of sight. Whoever's driving still feels like part of everything. With kids aboard, that mattered more than we expected.

features.title: A Cockpit That Feels Safe
features.description: Deep combings and bolsters enclose the seating area, wide side decks wrap all the way around, and the helm sits within the cockpit — slightly elevated for visibility but not up in the sky. Parents will understand immediately.
features.body:
Most of the catamarans we looked at put the cockpit right at water level or perched the helm way up on a flybridge — the first feels exposed, the second feels isolated. This design splits the difference. The cockpit is enclosed by proper combings and bolsters, wide side decks run all the way around, and the helm sits right there with everyone else, slightly elevated for sight lines but not up out of the conversation. Whoever's driving is still part of what's happening.

With kids on board, that mattered more than we expected.

- Deep combings and bolsters enclose the cockpit seating area
- Wide, walk-around side decks on both hulls
- Helm station within the cockpit — slightly elevated for visibility, but not separated
- Big sliding glass doors integrate the salon and cockpit into one space

## Meet the family behind the boat

We are Eric, Alex, Leon, and Margot — a family of four based in Madison, Wisconsin. This is our second Caribbean cruise. The first was ten months aboard a monohull we called [*Nethermead*](https://www.sailingnethermead.com/), from Miami to Grenada and back in 2021–2022. The kids were small, we had a great time, and when we came home we knew we wanted to do it again. For the second trip we wanted more space, more comfort, and a little more safety for the kids, so we sold *Nethermead* ourselves and bought [*Tropicalia*](https://sailingtropicalia.com/).

Eric earned a USCG 100-ton Master captain's license and has crossed the Atlantic twice. Alex had never sailed before she met him. Leon is nine. Margot is six.

We sold *Nethermead* FSBO and it was straightforward. We're doing the same here — we have lived aboard, maintained every system, and are happy to walk you through anything and put you in touch with the people we've worked with on the upgrades.

## Buying a Boat Directly from the Owner Private boat sales are common and straightforward. The process follows the same steps as a brokered transaction, but without the broker commission. Here is exactly what to expect. ## 1. Initial Contact [Reach out](/contact) to us. We are happy to answer questions, provide additional photos and videos, or schedule a video call to walk through the boat in real time. We encourage you to ask anything. ## 2. Offer & Deposit When you are ready to move forward, you submit a written offer using a standard marine purchase and sale agreement, much like you would do if you were making an offered on a brokerage boat. Once we reach agreement on terms, a refundable deposit (typically 10%) is placed into a licensed marine escrow account. This secures the boat and takes her off the market while you arrange a survey. ## 3. Marine Survey You hire a licensed marine surveyor of your choice. We will make the boat fully available for haul-out and inspection. The survey is your opportunity to have an independent professional assess every aspect of the vessel. ## 4. Sea Trial A sea trial is usually included as part of the survey process. You and your surveyor will be able to experience the boat under sail and power, test all systems, and get a feel for how she handles. We will be aboard to answer questions and demonstrate systems. ## 5. Acceptance of Vessel Once the survey and sea trial are complete, and if you are completely satisfied with what you find, you formally accept the vessel. If you are unsatisfied with the survey results, then you can walk away, and the escrow agent refunds your 10% deposit. ## 6. Closing The closing agent runs an abstract of title and lien search, prepares the bill of sale and USCG paperwork, holds the signed documents in escrow, confirms any prior liens or mortgages are satisfied, files the transfer with the USCG, and issues a new 5-year USCG Certificate of Documentation in the buyer's name. The buyer wires the balance of the purchase price into escrow, where it is held until the title transfer is confirmed and then released to the seller. Keys, manuals, and maintenance records pass to the new owner. We have closed two boats through [All Yacht Registries](https://allyachtregistries.com/) — the purchase of _Tropicalia_ and the private sale of _Nethermead_ — and were very satisfied with their professionalism on both transactions. Their [services and typical closing fees are outlined here](https://allyachtregistries.com/Fees.aspx): $750 base for a pleasure vessel, which we would split with you. They are our default recommendation, but the buyer is welcome to use any comparable closing and documentation service they prefer. ## Why FSBO Works Buying directly from the owner is not unusual in the marine world. Many experienced cruisers prefer it because they deal directly with someone who knows the boat intimately. There is no telephone game through a broker, and the savings on commission can be significant for both parties. ## Questions? If you have any concerns about the process, we are happy to discuss them. We want you to feel confident every step of the way. ## Sales Forms & Resources If you want to read through the standard paperwork ahead of time, YachtSite's Sales Forms page is a useful public resource — downloadable PDFs of the same templates a broker would walk you through, with a plain-language summary of how each step works. The forms most relevant to a sale like this one:

Offer Phase

  • Purchase & Sale Agreement
  • Acceptance of Vessel
  • Conditional Acceptance
  • Rejection of Vessel

faqs.question: What is a Voyage 500?
faqs.answer: The Voyage 500 is a 50-foot cruising catamaran designed by Simonis Voogd and built in South Africa by [Voyage Yachts](https://www.voyageyachts.com/), which has retired the 500 model but actively builds larger luxury cats. There is an active and supportive [Voyage Catamaran Owners Worldwide](https://www.facebook.com/groups/1614218135459635/) Facebook group. Voyage yachts are known for their solid build quality, comfortable living spaces, and strong bluewater sailing performance. The owner's version, like Tropicalia, is popular with long-range cruisers and liveaboards. Voyage also made a 4-cabin version of the 500, which was popular in the Caribbean charter circuit. Voyage has an active luxury crewed charter base in the Virgin Islands.

faqs.answer: Tropicalia is currently sailing in the British Virgin Islands. You can see our [live location on the About page](/about/), updated in real time via our PredictWind Hub over Starlink. We will be heading to Saint Martin and then south to Dominica and then north to Florida starting in May 2026. We are happy to arrange viewings at our current location or along our route.

faqs.answer: In short, our planned sailing sabbatical trip (the second one we've done with our young kids) is coming to an end. Tropicalia has been an amazingly comfortable and reliable platform for our adventures, but it has been our plan from the start to return to land life in Wisconsin. We hope the next owners enjoy her as much as we have.

faqs.question: How does the purchase process work?
faqs.answer:
We would use a standard marine purchase and sale agreement. Once we reach an accepted offer, the buyer places a 10% deposit into escrow to hold the boat and then conducts their survey and sea trial. If everything is to the buyer's satisfaction, they put the balance of the agreed-upon purchase price in escrow, and the escrow agent holds it until all contingencies have been met and the boat has been re-documented in the buyer's name. Once the USCG documentation paperwork has been submitted, the escrow agent releases the funds to the seller, and the transaction is complete.

We sold our last boat, a 2017 Hanse 415, this same way in 2022 — our [original FSBO listing site](https://hanseforsale.com/) is still online — and the entire transaction went smoothly. All the high-stakes parts of the transaction, like the search for liens, ownership verification, and escrow, are handled by a neutral third party closing agent, whose modest fee the buyer and seller would split. It allows us to not have to factor into the price the 10% commission a yacht broker typically takes.

faqs.question: Is a broker involved?
faqs.answer: This is a direct sale by owner. If you are working with a buyer's broker, we are open to cooperating with them. Please contact us to discuss the details.

faqs.question: Has the boat had any insurance claims?
faqs.answer: Yes. The boat was struck on the starboard sugar scoop by a motor yacht in a marina in 2023. It damaged the exterior fiberglass and starboard engine mounts. It was repaired at the St. Augustine Marine Center and covered by insurance. The previous owner's [damage disclosure statement is available for download](/documents/damage-disclosure.pdf).

faqs.question: What are the engine hours?
faqs.answer: The twin Yanmar 3JH5E engines have **3,323 hours on port** and **3,213 hours on starboard**. Both have been regularly serviced and run well, and were paired with brand-new Yanmar SD60 saildrives in 2025. We are still cruising, so these numbers will tick up modestly as we make our way back to St. Augustine. Note that the starboard Yanmar control panel was replaced; the hours displayed on that panel are lower than the actual engine total because there is no way to set a Yanmar hour meter to a non-zero value at install. We recorded the engine's true hours at the time of replacement, and the figure above reflects that running total.

faqs.question: Has the boat ever been chartered?
faqs.answer: Yes, but pretty lightly. The previous owner held the boat in an LLC and got it MARAD certified. He told us he did about three crewed day charters in Florida and specialized in ashes-spreading ceremonies at sea. The boat was not built for charter, nor did it ever have any overnight charter guests or do any bareboat chartering in Florida or anywhere else. The original owners never had the boat in charter.

faqs.question: When was the boat last hauled out?
faqs.answer: The boat was last out of the water at the St. Augustine Marine Center November 2025. As we wrap up our sailing sabbatical, we are heading back there for a June 17 haulout date.

faqs.question: What is the condition of the rigging?
faqs.answer:
The original owners would have the St. Augustine Marine Center pull the mast every year when they hauled the boat out there for hurricane season storage. The riggers there inspected the rig on the hard and replaced any components that exhibited wear. 

When we were considering the boat, we fully expected to replace the entire standing rigging as our first project, but we commissioned a [rigging report](/documents/rigging-report.pdf), which came out clean. Our insurers did not require new rigging, and our plans involved short island hopping, so we opted not to replace it right away. We've had no issues and would be very confident doing the same type of Caribbean trip on this rig. However, if we were to plan an ocean crossing, we would have it replaced.

faqs.question: In what condition are the sails?
faqs.answer:
When we purchased the boat, this was another item we expected to replace right away because the seller did not know when the sails had last been replaced. However, when we did the sea trial, we found the sails to be in better condition than expected, and we opted to hold off on replacement. 

I would categorize them as serviceable. The genoa still has quite good shape, and all sails are of  high-modulus cross-cut Dacron. The main's numerous full battens give it decent overall shape, but the leech is starting to look a little loose, and the UV covers on the genoa and storm jib need replacement. In my opinion, you can sail the islands for probably the next three years with these sails and do perfectly fine, but new canvas would likely add a half a knot of boat speed and be advisable if you are planning to cross any oceans.

faqs.question: How many owners has the boat had?
faqs.answer: We are the third owners. The original owners, who commissioned the boat from the Voyage factory, were a South African couple, one of whom was an aerospace engineer. The boat's original name was Panache, and we understand that they cruised it to the Caribbean each winter and hauled it out at the St. Augustine Marine Center each hurricane season. It was then purchased by a Florida resident (about 5 years ago) and renamed God's Grace. The second owner kept the boat in Florida, in the Gulf Coast area, and then back in St. Augustine. He made many upgrades and took much pride in ownership. He got the boat MARAD certified and ran a few day charter trips, mostly specializing the spreading of ashes at sea.

faqs.question: Are there any issues with the boat?
faqs.answer: Nothing major. We have tried our best to take great care of Tropicalia during our ownership, and we have upgraded a lot of systems to make her suited to our style of cruising. That said, every boat has issues, and we want you to know everything we know after living aboard for a year. All of it is spelled out in the [Known Issues & Disclosure](/documents/known-issues-disclosure.pdf) document.

faqs.question: Does the boat come with any spares?
faqs.answer: Yes! There are extensive spares, such as oil and fuel filters for the engines and generator, among many other spare parts and supplies for various systems. One of the first things we did when we took ownership of the boat was to go through all the spares and parts and organize and label them.

faqs.answer: Tropicalia was properly imported and is US Duty Paid.

faqs.question: What internet setup does the boat have?
faqs.answer: Tropicalia has Starlink satellite internet, which provides reliable broadband-speed connectivity virtually anywhere. We also have a backup 12V Starlink mini and voltage step-up converter still in the box. I worked part time from the boat during our trip without any connectivity issues.

faqs.answer: Yes. Dual-zone Mabru air conditioning: a 12,000 BTU unit (12V DC, soft start) serving the master cabin and salon, and a 17,000 BTU unit (120V, installed June 2024) serving the port hull and salon.
